The graph above shows the velocity of an object moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis. At time $t=3,$ the particle is located at the position $x=3.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=7?$

The position of the particle at $t=7$ is $x=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=7$ is equal to its position at $t=3$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [3,7].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(7)=x(3)+{\int }_{3}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

We are told that $x(3)=3$, and we can compute the integral ${\int }_{3}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t$ by finding the signed area under the graph from $t=3$ to $t=7.$ Computing the signed area, we get

$$
{\int }_{3}^{7}v(t)\,\text{d}t=8.
$$

Therefore,

$$
x(7)=3+8=11.
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=7$ is $x=11.$
